drivingQuestion: What does Rav Pappa's count of ten teach?
outcomeNote: Rav Pappa's count excludes R' Shimon's mixed offering

segments.he: גְּמָ׳ אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא: כֹּל הֵיכָא דִּתְנַן – עֶשֶׂר תְּנַן, מַאי קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן?
segments.en: «GEMARA:» «Rav Pappa stated» a principle with regard to all the mishnayot in tractate Menaḥot: «Anywhere that we learned» in a mishna that one brings a meal offering, «we learned» that one must bring «ten» items of the same type, either loaves or wafers. The Gemara asks: «What is» Rav Pappa «teaching us,» as this is already stated by Rabbi Yehuda in the mishna (76a)?

segments.he: לְאַפּוֹקֵי מֵרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן, דְּאָמַר: מֶחֱצָה חַלּוֹת וּמֶחֱצָה רְקִיקִין יָבִיא, קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן דְּלָא.
segments.en: The Gemara answers: This statement of Rav Pappa serves «to exclude» the opinion «of Rabbi Shimon, who said:» One who takes a vow to bring a meal offering baked in an oven must bring ten items. If he wishes, he may bring ten loaves or ten wafers, and if he wishes «he may bring half» of them as «loaves and» the other «half» as «wafers.» Rav Pappa «teaches us that» the tanna of the mishna maintains «that» one may «not» do so; all ten must be of the same type.
